name: Xue Mao Jiao (学猫叫)
blurb: A 2018 Chinese love song that went viral on Douyin with a cute cat-paw hand dance
title: Xue Mao Jiao (学猫叫): Who Sings It and Why It Went Viral on Douyin
description: Xue Mao Jiao (Learn to Meow) is a 2018 love song by Xiao Panpan and Xiao Fengfeng that went viral on Douyin with a cute cat-paw hand dance.
h1: What is the song "Xue Mao Jiao" (学猫叫)?
answer: Xue Mao Jiao (学猫叫, "Learn to Meow") is a sweet Chinese internet love song sung by Xiao Panpan (小潘潘) and Xiao Fengfeng (小峰峰), who wrote it, released in April 2018. On Douyin it was paired with a hand dance that copies a cat waving its paws; millions of users filmed their own versions in the summer of 2018, and celebrities such as Guan Xiaotong and Chen He joined in. It is one of the first big "Douyin hit songs" (抖音神曲).

body: The trend uses only the chorus and a hand dance: fists held up by the cheeks like cat paws, waved side to side in time with the beat, with a head tilt and a cute face. It is simple enough to do sitting down in front of a phone's front camera, so people filmed couple versions, pet versions and versions with their parents.

body.note: According to Chinese media reports from 2018, Xiao Panpan taught the hand dance on her livestreams after it took off, and tutorial videos passed 10 million views.

head: Date
Event
rows: Xiao Panpan and Xiao Fengfeng release the song (sources give dates between 20 and 23 April).
The first hand-dance video to the song appears on Douyin, passes a million views and is copied by many creators.
Media report the song has been used for hand-dance videos on Douyin more than 4 million times; its Weibo topic passes 100 million reads.
Celebrities including Guan Xiaotong, Chen He, Angelababy and Xu Zheng copy the dance; media call it a nationwide wave of acting cute.
It ranks 10th in Billboard Radio China's top 10 Chinese-language songs of 2018.

body: The song is sung as a girl being playful with her partner, promising to act like a kitten to win them over; "xue mao jiao" literally means "learn to meow", i.e. to meow and act cute.

Xiao Fengfeng has said he wrote it after a hard period trying to make music in Beijing, when his cat Tom fell seriously ill. He kept treating it, and when it recovered it kept meowing at him. The working title was simply "Mao Jiao" (Meow) before it became "Xue Mao Jiao".

A simple, bouncy, repetitive tune you can hum after one listen, plus a dance you learn in seconds, fit short video perfectly: easy to copy and easy to remix. Some critics dismissed it as a catchy but empty "earworm song", while lyricist Yao Qian compared its reach to the children's hit "Jiankang Ge" from about twenty years earlier. Today it is a nostalgic early-Douyin classic rather than a current trend.

faq.a: It is a duet by Xiao Panpan (小潘潘) and Xiao Fengfeng (小峰峰). Xiao Fengfeng wrote the words and music.

faq.q: How do you do the Xue Mao Jiao dance?
faq.a: Make two fists like cat paws, hold them beside your cheeks and wave them side to side on the beat, adding a head tilt and a wink. Repeat through the chorus.

faq.q: When did Xue Mao Jiao come out?
faq.a: In April 2018. It went viral on Douyin that summer.
